# @leadconnector/vite-plugin-dev-server-bridge

Vite development-server bridge for preview diagnostics, restart
notifications, and browser error collection.

## Usage

```ts
import { devServerBridgePlugin } from "@leadconnector/vite-plugin-dev-server-bridge";

export default {
  plugins: [devServerBridgePlugin()],
};
```

The plugin only applies to `vite serve`. Control request bodies time out after
2000ms by default and can be configured with
`controlBodyReadTimeoutMs`.

## Control routes

- `POST /__vibe/restart-announce`
- `GET /_sandbox/preview/viewers`
- `POST /_sandbox/preview/execute`

Restart and preview execution are delivered over Vite custom HMR events. The
injected restart client forwards `{ type: "VIBE_DEV_SERVER_RESTARTING" }` to
the parent frame.

Preview execution is limited to 50 KiB of UTF-8 code. Its timeout defaults to
1500ms and is clamped to 5000ms. Viewer results are normalized into bounded
JSON-wire-safe payloads before they are sent over HMR.

## Error collector

`devServerBridgePlugin()` enables browser error collection by default. The
collector route, `POST /__vibe/error-collector`, captures runtime errors,
failed resources, and unhandled promise rejections.

Reports are written as JSONL to `/tmp/vibe/runtime-errors.log`. The active log
and one deterministic rotation are each bounded to 1 MiB. Newly created output
directories and all log files use modes `0700` and `0600`; existing custom
parent directories are never chmodded. The plugin-owned default `/tmp/vibe`
directory is owner-checked before its mode is tightened. Parent directories
stay anchored by open descriptors. On Linux, traversal starts at an open root
descriptor and opens every component through `/proc/self/fd`; the complete
descriptor chain remains open for the server generation. Reset validates an
existing entry, unlinks it through the anchored parent, and creates a new
exclusive `0600` file. On Darwin, where Node does not expose `openat`, every
existing path component must be a real directory owned by the current user (or
a non-writable root-owned system directory); only known root-owned sticky
system temp directories may be writable. Darwin then keeps the validated parent
and file descriptors for the generation and does not reopen files for
mutation. Every log mutation rechecks that its descriptor is a regular file
owned by the current uid with exactly one hard link and exact mode `0600`.
When a successor server generation uses the same output, it retires the prior
generation before its serialized reset; already accepted writes finish first,
while later requests to the retired middleware are rejected. Symlink ancestors,
pre-planted hard links, replaced parents, and non-regular output targets are
rejected.

The Darwin fallback intentionally does not claim protection from a malicious
same-uid process racing path operations after descriptors are established;
its boundary blocks pre-planted links, unsafe ancestors, and other-user
storage. Retained logs are normalized from bounded tail reads, while reset
truncates directly without reading old content.
Oversized reports become complete `truncated-report` JSONL records rather than
partial byte slices.

```ts
devServerBridgePlugin({
  errorCollector: {
    endpoint: "/__vibe/error-collector",
    outputFile: "/tmp/vibe/runtime-errors.log",
    maxBodyBytes: 64 * 1024,
    bodyReadTimeoutMs: 2000,
    maxOutputBytes: 1024 * 1024,
    resetOnStart: true,
  },
});
```

Set `errorCollector: false` to disable collection. The collector can also be
used independently:

```ts
import { errorCollectorPlugin } from "@leadconnector/vite-plugin-dev-server-bridge";

export default {
  plugins: [errorCollectorPlugin()],
};
```
